# audio

PipeWire: output and input volume and mute, device lists, per-app streams and Bluetooth codecs.

```lua
list {
    items = mantle.audio:map(function(audio)
        return audio.sinks
    end),
    key = function(sink) return tostring(sink.id) end,
    each = function(sink)
        return rect {
            padding = 6,
            background = sink.active and "#45475A" or "#1E1E2E",
            on_click = function() mantle.audio:set_default_sink(sink.id) end,
            children = { text { content = sink.name } },
        }
    end,
}
```

## State

`mantle.audio:get()` returns `AudioState`, `nil` before the first push. A field marked `?` may be absent.

`mantle.audio`'s payload.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps` | `AppStream[]` | Apps playing or recording audio, excluding pid-less streams, notification sounds, meters and monitor captures. |
| `cards` | `AudioCard[]` | ALSA and BlueZ cards with their profiles, ordered by `device`. A card makes sinks and sources only for its active profile: analog or HDMI on one Intel HDA card, a codec on a headset. |
| `sinks` | `AudioDevice[]` | Every output device; the `active` one is the default. |
| `sources` | `AudioDevice[]` | Every input device; the `active` one is the default. |

### `AppStream`

One app's playback or recording stream. Streams without a pid are left out.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `binary?` | `string` | `application.process.binary`, e.g. `"firefox"`. |
| `icon?` | `string` | XDG icon name from `application.icon-name`, else `media.icon-name`, e.g. `"firefox"`. |
| `id` | `integer` | PipeWire node id, the first argument of `set_app_volume` and `set_app_muted`. |
| `media_name?` | `string` | `media.name`, which tells one app's streams apart, e.g. a browser tab's `"YouTube Music"`. Follows the stream as the client renames it. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | Stream mute; `false` until `volume` is known. |
| `name?` | `string` | `application.name`, if the client set one. |
| `pid` | `integer` | Owning process id, from `application.process.id`. |
| `process_name?` | `string` | `/proc/<pid>/comm`, or `nil` if it was unreadable when the stream's properties were read. |
| `recording` | `boolean` | A capture stream, such as a call's microphone, rather than playback. |
| `volume?` | `number` | Stream volume in percent; `nil` until PipeWire reports the stream's `Props`. |

### `AudioCard`

One ALSA or BlueZ card and every profile it offers.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active?` | `integer` | `index` of the active profile; `nil` before PipeWire reports it. |
| `device` | `integer` | PipeWire device id, the first argument of `set_card_profile`. |
| `mac?` | `string` | A BlueZ card's MAC address, from its `bluez_card.*` name with `_` turned to `:`; joins `mantle.bluetooth`. `nil` on an ALSA card. |
| `name` | `string` | `device.description`, e.g. `"Built-in Audio"`, else `device.nick`, else `device.name`. |
| `profiles` | `CardProfile[]` | Every profile, unavailable ones included, ordered by `index`. |

### `AudioChannel`

One sink or source channel. `position` is `nil` if PipeWire omits or does not name its channel map.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` | Zero-based index for `set_channel_volume`. |
| `position?` | `string` | Speaker position, e.g. `"front_left"` or `"front_right"`. |
| `volume` | `number` | Reported level in percent. Sink writes stop at `150`; only the default output is corrected above it. |

### `AudioDevice`

One `sinks` or `sources` entry.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | This is the default output or input; with no default known, or one not in this list, the lowest `id` is. |
| `balance?` | `number` | `-1.0` (left) to `1.0` (right); `nil` for mono, an unknown channel map, or before its first report. |
| `bus?` | `string` | `device.bus`, e.g. `"pci"`, `"usb"`, `"bluetooth"`. |
| `card?` | `integer` | The `cards[].device` this comes from; `nil` for a virtual device. |
| `channels?` | `AudioChannel[]` | Channel levels in percent, or `nil` before valid channel volumes arrive. Indices name the current channel order; read a fresh snapshot after a device changes. |
| `form_factor?` | `string` | `device.form-factor`, e.g. `"headset"`. |
| `icon?` | `string` | `device.icon-name` theme name, e.g. `"audio-card-analog"`. |
| `id` | `integer` | PipeWire node id, the first argument of every device action; not reboot-stable. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | `false` before its first report. |
| `name` | `string` | `node.description`, e.g. `"Built-in Audio Analog Stereo"`, else `node.nick`, else `node.name`. |
| `node_name` | `string` | `node.name`, e.g. `"alsa_output.pci-0000_00_1f.3.analog-stereo"`: stable across reboots, so a config keys its own labels on it. |
| `port?` | `string` | The active card route's `port.type`, e.g. `"headphones"`, `"hdmi"`, `"mic"`. |
| `volume?` | `number` | Volume in percent, the loudest channel; `nil` before its first report. A sink's default is pulled back to `150` when another client sets it louder. |

### `CardProfile`

One entry of `AudioCard.profiles`.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `available` | `boolean` | `false` when PipeWire reports the profile unavailable, such as HDMI with no display plugged in. |
| `codec?` | `string` | The Bluetooth codec the profile names, e.g. `"AAC"`, `"LDAC"`, `"mSBC"`; `nil` when it names none, as `off` and every ALSA profile. |
| `description` | `string` | PipeWire's description, e.g. `"Digital Stereo (HDMI) Output"`. |
| `index` | `integer` | Profile index, the second argument of `set_card_profile`. |
| `name` | `string` | PipeWire's untranslated id, e.g. `"output:hdmi-stereo"` or `"off"`. |

## Actions

Call each as `mantle.audio:<action>(arguments...)`; `?` marks an argument you may omit.

| Action | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set_volume` | `id: integer, volume: number` | Sets a `sinks[].id` or `sources[].id` volume in percent, clamped to `[0, 150]` for a sink and `[0, 100]` for a source. It need not be the default. |
| `set_muted` | `id: integer, muted: boolean` | Sets a `sinks[].id` or `sources[].id` mute. |
| `toggle_mute` | `id: integer` | Toggles a `sinks[].id` or `sources[].id` mute. |
| `set_balance` | `id: integer, balance: number` | Sets a `sinks[].id` or `sources[].id` balance, `-1.0` (left) to `1.0` (right), clamped; the louder side keeps its level. |
| `set_default_sink` | `id: integer` | Makes this `sinks[].id` the default output. |
| `set_default_source` | `id: integer` | Makes this `sources[].id` the default input. |
| `set_channel_volume` | `id: integer, index: integer, volume: number` | Sets one `channels[]` level of a `sinks[].id` or `sources[].id` in percent, clamped as `set_volume`. Other channels stay unchanged. |
| `set_app_volume` | `id: integer, volume: number` | Sets an `apps[].id` stream's volume in percent, clamped to `[0, 100]`. |
| `set_app_muted` | `id: integer, muted: boolean` | Sets an `apps[].id` stream's mute. |
| `set_card_profile` | `device: integer, index: integer` | Switches a `cards[].device` to one of its `profiles[].index`. WirePlumber keeps the choice. |

## Backend

PipeWire's native API, on one thread shared with [`privacy`](privacy.md#backend).

| PipeWire object | Feeds |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Audio/Sink`, `Audio/Source` nodes and the `default` metadata's `default.audio.sink`/`source` | `sinks`, `sources`, their `active`, `channels`, `volume`, `muted` and `balance`; `card` is the node's `device.id` |
| `Stream/Output/Audio`, `Stream/Input/Audio` nodes | `apps`, minus the streams its field lists |
| ALSA and `bluez_card.*` devices and their profiles | `cards`; a BlueZ card's `mac` comes from its name, a profile's `codec` from its name, else its English description |
| Each ALSA and BlueZ device's active `Route` | `port`, and a hardware sink's or source's volume, mute and balance, Bluetooth microphones included. The node's `Props` only mirror the `Route`: they are read until it arrives, and a write before then is dropped. A virtual device has no `Route` and uses its node's `Props` |

The first push waits until PipeWire has reported every object and its volume, so a machine with no
audio hardware still gets one push of empty lists. An unreachable PipeWire is logged and `audio`
stays `nil` until it comes up. A lost connection pushes empty lists, the same as no hardware. Either
way the Supervisor retries after 1 s, doubling to every 30 s, and the first push after it reconnects
is a full one.

Writes are not optimistic: state changes when PipeWire reports the new value. An action with no
target (a stale `id`, or a volume write or mute toggle before that device's first report) is dropped
with a `debug` log. Volume, mute and balance writes go to the device named, which need not be the
default.

## How do I…

### Change volume on the scroll wheel, mute on middle click

A handler reads with `:get()`: it needs the value now, not a binding ([input](../guide/input.md)).
The default output is the `active` entry of `sinks`.

```lua
local function default_sink(audio)
    for _, sink in ipairs(audio and audio.sinks or {}) do
        if sink.active then
            return sink
        end
    end
end

rect {
    on_wheel = function(_, steps)
        local sink = default_sink(mantle.audio:get())
        if sink == nil or sink.volume == nil then
            return
        end
        mantle.audio:set_volume(sink.id, math.max(0, math.min(100, sink.volume + steps * 5)))
    end,
    on_click = function(_, which)
        local sink = default_sink(mantle.audio:get())
        if which == "middle" and sink then
            mantle.audio:toggle_mute(sink.id)
        end
    end,
    children = {
        text {
            content = mantle.audio:map(function(audio)
                local sink = default_sink(audio)
                if sink == nil or sink.volume == nil then
                    return "--"
                end
                return sink.muted and "muted" or string.format("%d%%", math.floor(sink.volume + 0.5))
            end, "--"),
        },
    },
}
```

### Show an OSD when volume changes

`on_change` writes [named state](../guide/signals.md#named-state) that a panel binds, and a
[`timer`](../guide/scripting.md#timer) hides the panel again:

```lua
local osd_text = state("osd_text", "")
local osd_visible = state("osd_visible", false)
local hide_timer

local function default_sink(audio)
    for _, sink in ipairs(audio.sinks) do
        if sink.active then
            return sink
        end
    end
end

mantle.audio:on_change(function(audio, previous)
    local sink, before = default_sink(audio), previous and default_sink(previous)
    if before == nil or sink == nil or sink.id ~= before.id or before.volume == nil or sink.volume == nil then
        return -- the first push, or a new default, is learned state, not a change
    end
    if sink.volume == before.volume and sink.muted == before.muted then
        return
    end
    osd_text:set(sink.muted and "Muted" or string.format("Volume %d%%", math.floor(sink.volume + 0.5)))
    osd_visible:set(true)
    if hide_timer then
        hide_timer:cancel()
    end
    hide_timer = timer(2000, function() osd_visible:set(false) end)
end)

local osd = panel {
    id = "osd",
    layer = "overlay",
    anchor = { bottom = true },
    margin = { bottom = 80 },
    visible = osd_visible,
    padding = 12,
    radius = 12,
    background = "#1E1E2ECC",
    child = text { content = osd_text, font_size = 16 },
}
return osd
```

See also: [Volume OSD](../cookbook/volume-osd.md) recipe.
